story_type: giant machine moves ahead of a hurricane
hook: A hurricane was coming, so NASA moved a 400 foot tower.
narration: A hurricane was coming, so NASA picked up a four hundred foot tower and drove it away.
In August 2019, Hurricane Dorian was approaching, and this launch tower stood out at Pad 39B.
Crews at Kennedy Space Center sent crawler-transporter 2 to carry it.
The crawler rides on eight giant tracks. Machines like it hauled Saturn Fives and shuttles to the pad, at about a mile an hour.
The destination was the Vehicle Assembly Building, one of the largest buildings on Earth.
outcome: On August 30, the crawler rolled the launcher off Pad 39B and inside the Vehicle Assembly Building.
title: Moving a 400 ft tower from a hurricane
description:
Ahead of Hurricane Dorian, NASA's crawler-transporter 2 moved the nearly 400 foot tall Artemis mobile launcher from Launch Pad 39B to inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at Kennedy Space Center, Florida, on Aug. 30, 2019.
